messages:
Marta: quick flag -- we saw a subtle routing bug: Hosted assumed "capability names" were stable strings, Dedicated was publishing hyphenated keys and the runtime picked a fallback path.
Dev: can you paste an example of the mismatch?
Marta: example snippet from logs: `capabilities: ["quant-v2", "kv_cache"]` vs `capabilities: [{name:"quant",version:"2"}]`
Lin: we need a single canonical handshake shape. Proposal: manifest.v field (major int) + capabilities as list of objects {name, version, attrs}. Keep names stable and treat version as integer.
Omar: +1. Also recommend a lightweight capability hash so control-plane can diff quickly: `cap_hash = sha256(sorted(name+"#"+version))`. If mismatch, surface a telemetry event and don't silently degrade.
Marta: privacy concern: Private infra may not want full attrs exposed to Hosted. Proposal: manifest.expose_level: "none" | "hash_only" | "public". Default for Private is "hash_only".
Dev: how about failover policy? Hosted should not automatically failover to other modes if tenant sets expose_level=="none".
Lin: agree. Add handshake flag `failover_allowed: bool` that adapters set based on tenant policy. Control-plane enforces it.
Omar: implementation note: runtime adapters should return a minimal HTTP header `X-RW-MANIFEST-V` and `X-RW-CAP-HASH` during handshake to avoid parsing body on fast paths.
ControlBot: deploy-plan: manifest-schema-v1.1 draft published. review deadline 2026-04-05.
Marta: backward compatibility: if no manifest.v, treat as v0 and log an upgrade-needed metric. Old adapters continue to work but show as unverified.
Dev: tests: unit manifest parser, handshake e2e with simulated private bundles, and a routing smoke test to ensure no silent fallback.
Lin: I'll author the RFC with schema, header examples, privacy table, and rollout steps.
Omar: I'll add a lint rule in CI to check manifest headers.
Marta: thanks, keeping this tight so we can land in the next sprint. :thumbsup:
